title: Autopsy: detecting vulnerabilities in AI-generated code by reasoning across dependency graphs
description:
Autopsy is a static-plus-LLM vulnerability detector aimed at AI-generated code. It builds a cross-file dependency graph (Tree-sitter to NetworkX) over Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript, scans code in overlapping line windows so that large files are not limited by a single pass's output budget, and enriches every finding with a graph-derived blast radius: the set of callers that can reach the vulnerable function.

Alongside the LLM pass, Autopsy ships deterministic AST and graph detectors that require no model call and are scale-invariant: SQL strings interpolated into an execution sink, weak hashing of sensitive values, security gates whose return value is discarded, and deletion-based ("zero-footprint") vulnerabilities, where removing a comment boundary or a security control introduces a vulnerability that never appears as an added line in a diff.

This release is the reproducibility artifact accompanying the paper. It contains the detection pipeline, the benchmark harnesses (pygoat, SecurityEval, a Flask demo, and a TypeScript demo), the Semgrep, Bandit, and CodeQL security-extended baselines scored through a frozen matcher, the pre-registered matched-budget control, and the August 2026 replication with its qualitative failure analysis.
